Recent observations and model runs show no significant cooling trend or moisture influx that would cap the peak below 102°F or push it above 105°F, though minor forecast adjustments remain possible as the afternoon progresses. The broader 2026 summer pattern, with DFW tracking among the warmer Augests on record through mid-month, reinforces elevated baseline temperatures but does not alter the narrow range expected today. Resolution hinges on the official highest reading at the KDFW station, with updates from NOAA expected to refine the final value.

eventMetadata.context_description: Singapore's equatorial climate typically produces daily maximum temperatures near 31–32°C in mid-August, with limited day-to-day variability due to consistent humidity and sea-breeze effects. Recent drier conditions across the first half of the month, as noted in official advisories, have reduced cloud cover and allowed greater solar heating, supporting slightly elevated maxima around 33–34°C on several days, including a 34.6°C reading on August 16. Short-range forecasts for August 17 converge on 31–33°C, consistent with these patterns and historical August averages of roughly 88°F (31°C). Market-implied odds favoring 32°C (56%) and 33°C (32.5%) reflect trader consensus on this range, given the narrow spread of model guidance and the low probability of extremes outside recent observations.

Recent observations show the city has experienced variable conditions earlier in the month, including a cooler August 2 reading near 31–33°C tied to heavy rain; however, the latest model runs indicate drier, more stable air mass dominance for the 17th, supporting the clustered 36–38°C outcomes that together exceed 80% combined probability. Minor spread across 36°C (25.5%) and 38°C (16.5%) reflects remaining uncertainty in exact cloud cover, timing of any weak frontal passage, and localized urban heat-island effects. This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Kuala Lumpur Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 17 Aug '26.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus clusters tightly around 33–34°C because official forecasts from MET Malaysia and international models converge on daytime maxima in that narrow range for August 17 amid Kuala Lumpur’s equatorial climate, where strong solar insolation routinely drives highs near 32–33°C. Southwest monsoon conditions, moderate humidity, and typical afternoon cloud buildup or isolated showers limit further warming, while historical August averages hover around 32–33°C with rare excursions above 35°C. Minor model differences in timing of convective activity explain the near-even split between the two leading outcomes, with higher thresholds remaining low-probability absent an unexpected clear-sky anomaly.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) activity over Luzon remains the dominant driver, maintaining cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms that limit solar insolation and promote evaporative cooling in Metro Manila. Official PAGASA guidance for August 17 projects highs near 29–32 °C amid these conditions, consistent with historical August averages of ~30–31 °C that are frequently suppressed by monsoon cloud cover and moisture. Trader consensus, with 29 °C at 58.5 % and 30 °C at 35.5 % implied probability, reflects the expectation that widespread convective activity will keep maximum temperatures from exceeding the lower end of the seasonal range, while low-probability outcomes above 31 °C would require unexpected clearing or reduced rainfall. Updated model runs and the next PAGASA briefing will provide the key near-term data points.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 18 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: The southwest monsoon (habagat) currently dominating Luzon has sustained cloudy skies and scattered showers over Metro Manila, suppressing peak daytime heating and aligning with PAGASA's 25–29°C range forecasts for August 18. This pattern, typical of the wet season, reduces solar insolation relative to the seasonal 30–31°C average and keeps most model guidance clustered near 28–29°C maxima. Trader consensus reflects these conditions through the combined 82% implied probability on those two bins, with lower odds on 30°C+ outcomes hinging on any unexpected monsoon break. Updated PAGASA briefings and model runs over the next 48 hours remain the key near-term catalysts.
